verses.gurmukhi: ਰਾਜਾ ਪਰਜਾ ਹੋਇ ਕੈ ਚਾਕਰ ਕੂਕਰ ਦੇਸਿ ਦੁਹਾਈ।
verses.translit_en: raajaa parajaa hoi kai chaakar kookar dhes dhuhaiee|

en.bdb: By becoming subject of a king, people as servants go around the countries to abide orders.

verses.gurmukhi: ਜੰਮਦਿਆ ਰੁਣਿਝੁੰਝਣਾ ਨਾਨਕ ਦਾਦਕ ਹੋਇ ਵਧਾਈ।
verses.translit_en: ja(n)madhiaa runijhu(n)jhanaa naanak dhaadhak hoi vadhaiee|

en.bdb: On the birth of a child felicitatory songs are sung in the houses of the maternal and paternal grandfathers.

verses.gurmukhi: ਵੀਵਾਹਾ ਨੋ ਸਿਠਣੀਆ ਦੁਹੀ ਵਲੀ ਦੁਹਿ ਤੂਰ ਵਜਾਈ।
verses.translit_en: veevaahaa no siThaneeaa dhuhee valee dhuh toor vajaiee|

en.bdb: On marriage occasions the songs are sung by women in scurrilous language and trumpets are  played on the part of the bride and bridegroom (but not so among the gurmukhs).

verses.gurmukhi: ਰੋਵਣੁ ਪਿਟਣੁ ਮੁਇਆ ਨੋ ਵੈਣੁ ਅਲਾਹਣਿ ਧੁਮ ਧੁਮਾਈ।
verses.translit_en: rovan piTan muiaa no vain alaahan dhum dhumaiee|

en.bdb: Weepings and wailings are there for the dead;

verses.gurmukhi: ਸਾਧਸੰਗਤਿ ਸਚੁ ਸੋਹਿਲਾ ਗੁਰਮੁਖਿ ਸਾਧਸੰਗਤਿ ਲਿਵ ਲਾਈ।
verses.translit_en: saadhasa(n)gat sach sohilaa gurmukh saadhasa(n)gat liv laiee|

en.bdb: But the gurmukhs (the Guru-oriented) recite the Sohila in the company of the saints on such occasions.

verses.gurmukhi: ਬੇਦ ਕਤੇਬਹੁ ਬਾਹਰਾ ਜੰਮਣਿ ਮਰਣਿ ਅਲਿਪਤੁ ਰਹਾਈ।
verses.translit_en: bedh katebahu baaharaa ja(n)man maran alipat rahaiee|

en.bdb: The Sikh (gurmukh) goes beyond the holy books  of the Hindus and Muslims i.e. the Vedas and the Katebas, and neither rejoices at a birth nor mourns at a death.
In the midst of desires he remains free from them.
